text:
marta: Heads up — I'm about to change the inference svc to add a sidecar iptables-managed proxy for telemetry. Quick question: will that break the NLB health probe mapping if we change targetPort to the sidecar?
ryan: probably yes if probe hits the podIP:originalPort and sidecar binds a different port. what's the current Service manifest?
sophia: fwiw our last incident was because externalTrafficPolicy was Cluster and probe was routed to pods without the sidecar open port. We moved to Local to preserve node-level port mapping.
marta: here's the snippet from my terraform k8s_manifest resource:```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-svc
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
spec:
  type: NodePort
  externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
  selector:
    app: inference
```
todd: so probe is hitting node:health-port -> NodePort -> randomly to a pod; if sidecar is on 15001 and the app is on 8080, the probe will fail unless we expose 8080 on the pod IP.
ryan: options: 1) keep targetPort as app port and let sidecar transparently proxy (requires iptables TPROXY or redirect); 2) change Service targetPort to sidecar port (15001) and update liveness/readiness probes in pod; 3) change externalTrafficPolicy to Local and ensure nodeport routes to nodes running the pod, but still need matching ports.
sophia: (2) is simplest short-term: set targetPort to 15001 and update probes in deployment to call localhost:15001 -> sidecar will forward to app. But that changes semantics for intra-cluster dns -> podIP:8080. Might break other things.
marta: I don't want to touch app code. prefer limited kube-level changes. Could we instead add a headless svc for internal podIP:8080 traffic and keep main svc pointing at sidecar?
todd: headless svc could work for pod-to-pod DNS. You'd then have two svcs: inference-internal (ClusterIP None -> targetPort 8080) and inference (NodePort -> targetPort 15001).
ryan: also consider setting annotation `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-port` to the NodePort so ELB probes node:nodeport. That avoids pod port mismatch.
marta: ah good call. Is that annotation supported for NLB? I think it's `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-nodeport`?
sophia: there's `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-port` that accepts a port or "traffic-port". For NLB we can use `healthcheck-port: "traffic-port"` or explicit NodePort. Docs: https://kubernetes-sigs.github.io/aws-load-balancer-controller/latest/annotations/service/
ryan: quick checklist before I approve the TF PR: - add headless svc for internal traffic OR update internal consumers to internal svc name - decide targetPort for public svc (app vs sidecar) - set healthcheck-port annotation to nodeport or traffic-port - confirm externalTrafficPolicy (we usually prefer Local for LB health semantics)
marta: opened the PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/432 - changes are in modules/k8s/inference/service.tf, adds headless svc, sets targetPort 15001, and annotation `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-port: "traffic-port"`.
deploy-bot: CI passed for PR #432 — terraform plan OK (no drift). :white_check_mark:
todd: quick review: lgtm except we should add a note in the chart values that internal clients should use inference-internal.default.svc.cluster.local. Also add a readiness probe tweak so sidecar waits for app socket.
sophia: also add to runbook: how to rollback if sidecar crashes (iptables rules might persist on node?).
marta: thanks — I'll add docs and the readiness tweak. If everyone OK I'll merge after a short canary. :thumbsup:
ryan: :eyes: I'll watch the canary. If we see 5xx from requests, I'll open a rollback.
marta: merging in 10m unless objections.
todd: no objections.
sophia: no objections.
ryan: ack.
marta: merged and canary started — linking k8s events: kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=inference -o wide
marta: followup: we saw minor probe flapping on one node, cordoned and drained, it recovered. Observability shows a small latency bump (100ms) during rollout. All good now. :white_check_mark:
